passage.title: SHARING A FLAT IN EDINBURGH
passage.subtitle: Life with a flatmate
paragraphs: Six months ago, Maya and her university friend Chloe decided to rent a bright second-floor flat in Edinburgh. Both girls wanted to live close to the city library, and their new street is only a ten-minute walk from campus.

The flat has two small bedrooms, a sunny kitchen, one bathroom, and a comfortable living room. In the living room, there is a soft grey sofa, a wooden coffee table, and a tall bookshelf next to the window. Maya brought three green plants from her parents' house to make the room look nicer.

Living together works well because they share the housework fairly. Maya loves cooking, so she usually prepares dinner on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Chloe prefers cleaning; she sweeps the floors and washes the dishes after meals. At weekends, they sometimes invite friends over for board games.
Sometimes the street outside is noisy on Saturday nights, but Maya and Chloe don't mind. They say their flat is warm, cosy and much cheaper than living alone.
